schema.label: 1017 Brick Squad / Asylum / Warner Bros. Records

paras: “No Hands” — produced by Drumma Boy, featuring Roscoe Dash and Wale — was released on 17 August 2010 as a single from Waka Flocka Flame’s debut Flockaveli. It peaked at No. 13 on the Billboard Hot 100, has sold more than ten million units, and in 2023 became his first RIAA Diamond single. It is the plaque hanging on Patchwerk’s wall.

paras.caption: The Triple Platinum “No Hands” award on Patchwerk’s plaque wall, presented by Warner Bros. Records for RIAA-certified sales of more than 3,000,000 digital downloads of the single.

paras: Patchwerk’s only sheet naming “No Hands” is dated 23 August 2010, Studio 1019, engineer Brian Friesen, logged as “Copy backup Song No Hands / Backup DVD Copy — No Hands” — half an hour, made six days after the single came out.

The song the sheets actually document, session after session, is the record’s earlier single: “O Let’s Do It.” Between November 2009 and March 2010, engineer Kori Anders — spelled “Anders” on some sheets, “Andes” on others — logged five sessions in Studio 995 naming it directly: clean edits, a remix, a video-edit pass, and a 29 January 2010 recall whose project line explains an extra hour in his own hand: “Had to wait for P. Diddy to approve all changes.” Diddy guests on the official remix alongside Rick Ross and Gucci Mane — that sheet is the paper trail for getting the verse signed off. An earlier sheet, 12 November 2009, logs the same engineer and room for “Ruff mixes” with the title field blank.

sections._NOTE: Each answer leads with a complete, standalone fact naming the song, artist and studio, so it reads correctly when quoted in isolation. These cards also feed the FAQPage structured data.

items.q: Was Waka Flocka Flame’s “No Hands” recorded at Patchwerk Recording Studios?
items.a: Patchwerk Recording Studios’ only documented session for “No Hands” is dated 23 August 2010: engineer Brian Friesen spent thirty minutes in Studio 1019 making a “Backup DVD Copy” of the song, six days after its 17 August release. The song itself — produced by Drumma Boy, featuring Roscoe Dash and Wale — is now RIAA Diamond-certified with more than 10 million units sold.

items.q: Where was Waka Flocka Flame’s “O Let’s Do It” recorded?
items.a: “O Let’s Do It” was worked on at Patchwerk Recording Studios across five sessions that name it directly between January and March 2010, all in Studio 995 with engineer Kori Anders (the sheets spell it both “Anders” and “Andes”). An earlier sheet, 12 November 2009, logs the same engineer and room for “Ruff mixes” with no title on the sheet. The named sessions run from clean edits through a full remix to a video-edit pass, more studio time than any other Waka Flocka song in Patchwerk’s records.

items.q: Why does a Waka Flocka Flame session report mention P. Diddy?
items.a: A 29 January 2010 Patchwerk session report for the “O Let’s Do It” remix explains a scheduling delay in the engineer’s own handwriting: “# Had to wait for P. Diddy to approve all changes is the reason for the extra hour.” Diddy features on the official remix alongside Rick Ross and Gucci Mane, and this recall session — logged at four hours instead of the usual three — is Patchwerk’s paper trail for getting his verse signed off.

items.q: What does the Waka Flocka Flame plaque at Patchwerk commemorate?
items.a: The framed award on Patchwerk’s wall is a Triple Platinum plaque presented to Patchwerk Recording Studios by Warner Bros. Records, commemorating RIAA-certified sales of more than 3,000,000 digital downloads of the 1017 Brick Squad / Warner Bros. single “No Hands” featuring Roscoe Dash and Wale. The song has since been upgraded to Diamond status for surpassing ten million units.

sections.body: “No Hands” became Waka Flocka Flame’s signature record and, in 2023, his first Diamond single — but Patchwerk’s own paperwork for it is a half-hour backup copy dated six days after release. The real studio time went to “O Let’s Do It,” five sessions deep by name, plus an earlier sheet naming the same engineer and room for “Ruff mixes,” with a handwritten note explaining why they were waiting on P. Diddy.

note: Engineering credits shown are drawn directly from Patchwerk’s own session logs; only Patchwerk’s documented contributions are listed here. The 12 November 2009 session was photographed twice in the archive and is counted once.
